newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Euro Social Democrats gather in jubilant mood.
newsitem.headline: Euro Social Democrats gather in jubilant mood.

text.p: European Social Democrats met in jubilant mood on Thursday, announcing the end of right-wing politics as new centre-left leaders stepped onto the international stage for the first time.

"People have turned their backs on right-wing experiments. We must meet the expectations that people around Europe place on us, to take responsibility for jobs, peace and stability and a better environment," said Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson.
Nine of the European Union's 15 prime ministers have gathered in this southern Swedish city for a European Social Democratic party congress, reflecting the new face of Europe.

Since Tony Blair's Labour Party won the British election and Lionel Jospin's socialists followed with a ' win in the French election last weekend, 13 of the 15 EU member states are governed by centre or centre-left administrations.
"We are here in Malmo to lay the foundations for a democratic and new Europe," said Rudolf Scharping, President of the Party of European Social Democrats.

But the shadow of the European Union's single currency hung over the conference, with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Persson sparring at a news conference about Sweden's decision not to join economic and monetary union.
"I would have been pleased with a different decision," Kok told a news conference.
But Kok said there was little the EU could do to force Sweden to join EMU. "We're not going to call the police and the fire brigade out," he said.
The congress is seen as an ideal opportunity for the social democratic leaders to harmonise their ideas ahead of an EU summit in Amsterdam on June 16/17.

Wide discrepancies still exist between some of the parties on issues like labour market reform. Persson said employment was one of the key issues to be addressed, along with the environment, education and EU enlargement.
"Today political forces that will lead Europe into the 21st century are meeting in Malmo," Persson told the 1,000 delegates attending the three-day conference.

It was the first time that newcomers Blair and Jospin have appeared on the international stage together. Both will address the congress on Friday morning. On Thursday they were in bilateral discussions.
